title: RigidBody.freeze causes _input_event and _mouse_enter/exit to be calculated from incorrect location
body:
### Tested versions

v4.6.2.stable.official [71f334935]

### System information

Godot v4.6.2.stable - Windows 11 (build 26200) - Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060 Laptop GPU (NVIDIA; 32.0.15.8097) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i9-14900HX (32 threads) - 31.62 GiB memory

### Issue description

When calling `freeze = true` on a RigidBody, and afterwards manipulating the objects position, the callbacks `_input_event`, `_mouse_enter` and `_mouse_exit` will use the *position of the object when it was frozen*, instead of it's updated position.

**Example use-case:** Picking up a Rigid body, freezing it, and having it track to the mouses position, until you release: then unfreeze, and let it simulate physics again. 

This bug is reproducible in both Godot physics and Rapier2D. Bug is reproducible regardless of the freeze mode. Bug is reproducible regardless of whether I call `freeze = true` or `set_defered("freeze", true)

The bug is a bit "shy" and can fail to show up, if there is additional stuff going on. For example even just changing the position of an unrelated object when freezing the rigid body causes the bug not to appear.





### Steps to reproduce

**Instructions for MRP:**

1. Set Debug-> Visible Collision Shapes if not already on. Click play.
2. Left click (and hold) to move the ball to a new location. Ideally you should be able to release left click wherever you want, to drop the ball. 
3. Instead, observe that releasing left click does nothing, *unless* you are still hovering over the location where the rigid body _was_ when you picked it up.
4. You can view the logs for "Mouse enter" and "Mouse exit" to see how they are printing incorrectly (as if the rigid body was still where it started)

IMPORTANT: If you open the `ball.gd` file, there are some lines you can uncomment inside of the `attach_to_mouse` function. These lines were intending to make the MRP easier to understand, but they actually cause the bug not to be reproducible. 

In other words, setting the position of an unrelated object causes the bug to dissapear.


### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[repo_physics_bug_2026-05-12_10-10-36.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/27626763/repo_physics_bug_2026-05-12_10-10-36.zip)
